newsitem.title: USA: Texas Industries marketing CemStar process.
newsitem.headline: Texas Industries marketing CemStar process.

text.p: Texas Industries Inc said Monday it is marketing a proprietary cement manufacturing process called CemStar.
It said the CemStar process has demonstrated its ability to increase cement plant capacity between 5 and 15 percent.
The patented process uses "slag," steel making by-product. By adding the slag into a cement kiln with other feedstock materials, total production capacity of the kiln is increased.
The cement produced is the same quality Portland cement as that made with standard raw materials, Texas Industries said.
"CemStar has increased TXI's production by an average of 9 percent over last year at the company's two plants," stated Robert D. Rogers, president.
"Unquestionably, CemStar has contributed to TXI's record earnings over the last year," Rogers said.
Noting "we expect to increase" the percentage production rise, he said "Without doubt, CemStar can expand cement production at the lowest investment cost.
"Conventional methods of increasing plant capacity require high capital expenditures," he pointed out. "CemStar avoids these costs."
A subsidiary, CemStar Inc, has been formed to market and license the product worldwide.
"Our next objective is to license CemStar to other cement companies in the U.S. and internationally," Rogers said.
A licensing agreement with North Texas Cement Co has been concluded and negotiations with other cement companies are in process, he said.
CemStar was conceived more than 2 years ago through the joint efforts of Texas Industries and its 84 percent owned affiliate, Chaparral Steel Co.

"Developing new ideas for recycling has been a key strategy for both TXI and Chaparral," continued Rogers. "With CemStar, cement production is increased with the additional positive environmental benefits of reducing per unit fuel consumption and recycling slag."
Currently, slag utilization is generally limited to road base, fill material and railroad ballast, the company noted.
